business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Transactional Email API and Newsletter Hosting Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (hybridized with EU supranational law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L561-1 to L561-57 and R561-1 et seq.; Ordonnance n°2016-1635 of 1 December 2016; Décret n°2016-1123 of 10 August 2016; Code de commerce Article L123-23 and R123-166-1 (UBO registration with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); AMF General Regulation, ACPR Instruction 2020-D-12 (AML/CFT homologation).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport (or national ID) of each direct shareholder and natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent administrative authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing for corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of financial solvency for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in the shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (Statuts) duly notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French notary (Notaire) or certified legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization (only if notarized outside France)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory ongoing screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and commercial counterparties against the French Treasury (Tracfin) filings, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List when any U.S. nexus exists; Politically Exposed Person (PEP) risk scoring under Article L561-10 of the French Monetary and Financial Code and ACPR/AMF guidelines; enhanced due diligence mandated for UBOs resident in high-risk third countries as defined by FATF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises via https://procedures.inpi.fr (INPI), supplemented by RCS availability search through Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and INPI prior-mark search (https://data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be legible in the French Latin alphabet; foreign names must be transliterated into Latin characters and conform to French typing conventions. The name must be sufficiently distinctive and not misleadingly similar to existing registered names or trademarks in France. The mandatory legal form suffix 'SARL' must appear in all corporate acts and on all external correspondence.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France / National / Républicain (ministerial authorization required when suggesting public patronage)
Université / Institut / Académie (protected words requiring higher-education regulatory approval)
Police / Gendarmerie / État / Ministère (state-immunity and public-order restrictions)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS or INPI rejection based on confusion with an existing identical or similar name, the applicant may file a written administrative challenge before the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days stating grounds of non-confusion and evidencing intellectual-property search results; if the Greffier maintains the refusal, the applicant may bring a summary proceeding before the Président du Tribunal de Commerce (référé) for authorisation to register the name. For refusal based on a prior trademark, the applicant may also instigate cancellation or invalidation proceedings before the INPI or the French courts. All appeals must be submitted in French through a licensed avocat registered with a French bar.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible within statutory limits: a SARL may validly establish its registered office at a licensed 'domiciliation' business center (agréé) subject to an approved domiciliation contract, but an operational business address must exist in France for tax and postal purposes; the email/newsletter infrastructure may be hosted abroad, but the legal seat and effective management control should remain identifiable in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: Low to Moderate for an email-infrastructure SaaS; statistical expectancy of 5–10% within the first operating year due to VAT registration and anti-fraud checks by DGFiP and URSSAF.

RCS registration fee, Kbis issuance, and UBO register filing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL), L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company law), R.123-30 et seq. (RCS), and implementing Decree n° 2021-300 (Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises); legal publicity governed by Decree n° 67-236.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office arrondissement; filings are submitted through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INSEE with transmission to the Greffe, DGFiP and URSSAF.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company registration file consisting of the M0/MBO declaration (formulaire M0), certified articles of association (statuts), proof of publication in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL), capital deposit attestation and registered office consent; final proof of registration is the Extrait K-Bis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital for SARL; the articles of association freely fix the amount. All shares must be fully subscribed by the associates, and each cash contribution must be paid in to at least 20% at incorporation (Article L.223-7, Code de commerce), with the remaining 80% payable within five years. The paid-up sums must be deposited and blocked on a dedicated company account opened with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC), released only upon presentation of the K-Bis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST MEETING OF THE ASSOCIATES AND APPOINTMENT OF THE GÉRANT
The associates, having subscribed the entire share capital, hereby resolve:
1. Adopt the draft articles of association and the corporate purpose of email infrastructure services.
2. Confirm that at least twenty per cent of each cash subscription is deposited on the blocked company account.
3. Fix the registered office at the address stated in the articles, subject to RCS jurisdiction.
4. Appoint the Gérant with full administrative powers to bind the company.
5. Authorize the Gérant to publish the legal notice, file the incorporation dossier with the Guichet Unique, and complete all tax and registry formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Associates acting by private deed (sous seing privé); notary optional unless a real-property contribution is made; contribution auditor (commissaire aux apports) engaged where statutory valuation thresholds apply.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts in French containing the corporate name, SARL legal form, registered office located within a single RCS jurisdiction, corporate object limited to ISIC 6201 email-infrastructure SaaS services, share capital, division into shares, cash contribution schedule, appointment of the Gérant and 99-year duration. All associates or their duly authorized representatives must sign every page and the final page. If non-cash contributions exist, attach the contribution valuer's report. Ensure the cash payment schedule complies with the 20% minimum paid-up rule of Article L.223-7, Code de commerce.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of each associate or legal entity shareholder
Draft articles of association in French
Registered office lease or attestation de jouissance
Power of attorney where an associate signs through a representative
Contribution valuer's report (if in-kind contributions are made)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe returns a rectification notice, amend the defective clauses, re-execute the statuts with all associates, and resubmit the amended version through the Guichet Unique within the statutory correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Blocking Deposit and Opening of the Company Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed credit institution (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale, or regulated online business bank) or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name 'FR_SARL en formation' with a complete KYC file. Transfer the cash contributions representing at least 20% of each subscribed cash portion, ensuring the sums are exclusively credited to the business. Obtain the bank's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming that the funds are irrevocably held until presentation of the K-Bis. This certificate must be appended to the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Provisional or final articles of association
Identity documents of all associates and the intended Gérant
KYC documentation and source-of-funds evidence
Bank account opening mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the blocking certificate, deposit the funds with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or with a notary escrow, and tender the substituted certificate to the Greffe together with the initial bank refusal letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal-notices newspaper (Journal d'Annonces Légales) duly authorized in the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the chosen JAL to publish the statutory announcement containing the corporate name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office address, corporate object (bulk transactional email API and newsletter hosting), surname and first name of the Gérant, duration, and the city of the RCS where registration will occur. Pay the publication fee and collect the original attestation de parution (proof of publication), which is a mandatory annex of the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Text of the intended legal announcement
Corporate identification data (name, capital, registered office, manager)
Proof of payment of publication fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL refuses the announcement for formatting errors or incomplete mandatory mentions, correct the announcement text in accordance with the legal publication rules and republish; the corrected attestation de parution must then be submitted with the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Dossier Submission through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with transmission to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, DGFiP and URSSAF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet Unique portal and select the creation of a SARL. Complete the M0/MBO declaration collecting company identity, registered office, share subscription schedule, Gérant designation and place of RCS registration. Upload the signed articles of association, the JAL publication attestation, the capital blocking certificate, the registered office occupancy document, identity documents of all natural persons involved, and the declaration of absence of criminal convictions. Submit the electronic file; the Greffe of the competent commercial court performs the conformity review and notifies the applicant of any mandatory adjustments.
required_dossiers: Completed M0/MBO registration form
Signed and fully executed articles of association
Attestation de parution from the Journal d'Annonces Légales
Capital deposit and blocking certificate issued by the bank or CDC
Registered office lease or occupancy consent
Identity documents of all associates and the Gérant
Declaration on honour of non-conviction (casier judiciaire)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a 'demande de complément' or a rejection, the filer may rectify incomplete items online and resubmit within the 15-day procedural deadline; if the Greffe refuses registration on legal grounds, the applicant may petition the President of the Commercial Court in urgent proceedings (référé) for an order compelling registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration, Issuance of Extrait K-Bis and Company Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); INSEE for SIREN/SIRET allocation; DGFiP for fiscal and VAT enrolment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After conformity verification, the Greffe registers the SARL in the RCS and issues the Extrait K-Bis, which serves as conclusive proof of legal existence. The K-Bis contains the SIREN and SIRET numbers; the Guichet Unique automatically notifies URSSAF and DGFiP, triggering social security and tax registration. The company may then open its definitive operating bank account, release the blocked capital, and commence commercial activity.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique validation notice and filing receipt
K-Bis extract request confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory turnaround is exceeded, submit a formal reminder to the Greffe or lodge an application before the Juge du Registre to compel registration; if substantive defects in the articles are discovered post-registration, modify the articles by an extraordinary shareholders' meeting and refile the amending resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Data Protection and Tax Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGFiP (Centre des Impôts), URSSAF, and CNIL (Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés) for processing of newsletter subscriber personal data.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the K-Bis and verify that the company has been automatically enrolled for corporate income tax, VAT and employer obligations. If required by the activity, file a data-processing declaration with CNIL or execute the mandatory AIPD/DPIA for the transactional email platform, appoint a Data Protection Officer where the processing volume exceeds thresholds. After activation of the SIREN, configure the email infrastructure (SPF, DKIM, DMARC records) and finalize the GDPR compliance documentation for clients.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-Bis and SIREN notification
DGFiP tax and VAT registration references
CNIL declaration form or DPIA documentation as applicable
Email infrastructure technical configuration plan (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or employer references are incorrect, request correction through the DGFiP online professional space; if the CNIL file is rejected, reformulate the processing description and refile; technical configuration failures are cured by adjusting DNS records and re-running deliverability tests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board for purely digital ISIC 6201 businesses in France. Sector policy supervision is exercised by the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE), while data protection activity is overseen by the CNIL.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required (unlicensed activity). Recommended voluntary certifications for email infrastructure credibility: ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and CNIL registration for newsletter data processing. Transactional email transmission does not constitute a telecommunications activity requiring an ARCEP licence under the Code des postes et des communications électroniques.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique et de la Cohésion des Territoires / ADEME (advisory and compliance guidance) — no project-level environmental authorization applies to a software-only service activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure software-as-a-service activity under ISIC 6201 with no Classified Installation for Environmental Protection (ICPE); a full EIA or registration is triggered only if the company self-operates physical data centres above the thresholds of Article R.511-9, Code de l'environnement, or engages in hardware manufacturing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater, VOC or particulate discharges for the email API and newsletter hosting activity. Where the company contracts EU data-centre capacity, it shall contractually require hosts to comply with the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for e-waste, the RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU, Electromagnetic Compatibility Directive 2014/30/EU, and the French data-centre environmental decree n° 2021-1525 setting minimum transparency and impact thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office-only occupancy prevails: no public-assembly fire certification (commission de sécurité ERP) is required for non-ICP business offices. The company must nevertheless maintain workplace fire-safety compliance under the Code du travail (evacuation plan, emergency lighting, smoke detectors, fire-fighting equipment), keep a registre de sécurité, obtain an electrical conformity attestation per NF C 15-100, comply with occupational health monitoring (médecine du travail) for employees, and carry adequate civil liability insurance for property and personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the Ministry for Economy and Finance; professional tax portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel / EDI-TVA). Company formation and tax-identification filings are lodged through the single window Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the French SARL, the M0 filing through the Guichet Unique automatically triggers INSEE registration (SIREN/SIRET) and DGFiP issuance of the French VAT number in the format FR + two-digit control key + nine-digit SIREN. A non-resident enterprise without a French establishment must apply to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) or the Centre des Impôts des Non-Résidents (Noisy-le-Grand) using the SIFI fast-track procedure or Form 3310-CA3 before the first taxable transaction; VAT numbers are typically issued within one to two weeks for SIFI filings. The SARL's primary corporate income tax account is managed by the competent SIE based on the registered office location.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Article 206(1) CGI on worldwide profits, with a foreign permanent establishment exclusion option under Articles 209 and 214 CGI. There is no automatic pass-through unless a valid transparency election is made. France applies no sub-national income tax; the territorial scope is unitary at national level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections include: (i) five-year transparency election to be taxed as a partnership (impôt sur le revenu) under Article 239 bis AA CGI for SARLs with fewer than 50 individual shareholders and an industrial, commercial, artisan, agricultural or liberal activity; (ii) election for foreign permanent establishment net-exemption under Articles 209/214 CGI; (iii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C III CGI for closely linked resident entities; (iv) OSS/IOSS/PPP schemes for EU distance sales and B2C electronic services; (v) ATAD hybrid and reverse-hybrid reporting via annual Form 2258-SD with interest deduction limitation under Article 212 bis CGI and CFC rules under Article 209 B CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA) governed by Articles 256 to 298 sexdecies M of the French General Tax Code and Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold applies to an established French SARL: VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction and is obtained at incorporation (SIREN/VAT number). For foreign suppliers established outside France supplying B2C digital services ('services électroniques'), the EU-wide distance-sales threshold for use of the OSS scheme is EUR 10,000 annual turnover (Article 298 sexdecies F CGI); above that threshold, the place of supply is the consumer's Member State and the supplier must register or use OSS. Since the Email_Infra_SaaS activity is predominantly B2B, most supplies will be subject to reverse-charge in the customer's jurisdiction, with no French output VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured e-invoicing under the facturation électronique reform: from 1 September 2026 all VAT-registered businesses must be able to receive B2B electronic invoices and large enterprises must issue through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDP) or the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF); from 1 September 2027 mid-caps and SMEs (including this SARL) must issue. B2C transactions are subject to monthly e-reporting of transaction and payment data with a maximum transmission delay of 30 days. Mandatory formats are Factur-X, UBL and CII. There is no digital stamping and no real-time fiscal clearance comparable to the Italian SDI; however, anti-fraud cross-matching is performed on transmitted data, and non-compliance triggers penalties up to EUR 15,000 per infringing invoice under Article 1737 CGI.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports outside the EU qualify for the 0% (exonération) rate under Article 262-I-1 CGI, subject to proof of physical export being established within 90 days of dispatch (Article 74 Annexe III CGI). For services, the email-API and newsletter hosting platform constitutes electronically supplied services; B2B supplies are excluded from French VAT by place-of-supply rules (Article 259-1 CGI) and are subject to reverse charge in the customer's country, B2C supplies to EU consumers are taxed at the destination Member State's rate via OSS, and B2C supplies to non-EU consumers fall outside the French territorial scope under Article 259 C CGI. No French VAT is therefore chargeable on export services, provided the SARL maintains documentary evidence of the customer's business status, establishment and actual consumption location.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAU (Déclaration Administrative Unique) — electronic export declaration lodged via the DELTA/GUN customs clearance system
Commercial invoice with export references, Incoterms and zero-rating legal basis
Bill of Lading, air waybill or CMR transport document evidencing physical dispatch from the EU (for goods)
Customs exit confirmation or visa record proving goods left the EU within the 90-day deadline
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de change) or SWIFT credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP audit rights follow the standard three-year limitation (Article L.169 LPF), extended to six years for undeclared or partially declared activity and ten years for arrangements involving undeclared foreign accounts or offshore assets. Where export zero-rating or off-scope treatment is not substantiated, VAT is re-assessed at 20% with late interest of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI) and penalties of 40% for bad faith (Article 1729(a) CGI) or 80% for fraudulent maneuvers (Article 1729(b) CGI). Fraudulent export declarations additionally trigger customs sanctions under Articles 413-1 and 414 of the Code des Douanes, including confiscation of goods, fines up to three times the value of the fraud object, suspension of export privileges, and criminal liability; the SARL's legal representative may also be held personally liable for deliberate tax offenses under Article L.267 LPF.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is France's national central bank and part of the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR), hosted by the Banque de France, supervises French credit institutions and certain payment institutions. The Direction générale du Trésor administers French external financial-relations rules and related reporting under the Monetary and Financial Code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is in the euro area. The euro is freely convertible for current and capital transactions, subject to EU and French sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax rules, and applicable statistical or regulatory reporting. No general exchange-control approval is required for a French SARL to receive foreign investment, hold foreign-currency accounts, pay non-resident suppliers, or remit dividends abroad. Dividend distributions remain subject to distributable-profits, corporate approval, withholding-tax, treaty, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse requirements. Banks may require evidence of the transaction's commercial or investment purpose and source of funds. Transfers involving sanctioned persons, restricted jurisdictions, or controlled goods and services may be prohibited or require authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general export-proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in euros or foreign currency, subject to contractual terms, sanctions, tax, accounting, and applicable reporting requirements. The French Monetary and Financial Code contains reporting obligations for certain cross-border transactions and foreign assets; thresholds, exemptions, and filing procedures should be checked for the transaction and reporting period. Cash physically entering or leaving the EU with a value of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared to customs. This cash declaration is not a surrender or bank-transfer rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account where required for formation or a specific capital transaction
Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account where required for formation or a specific capital transaction

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account subject to the selected caisse's services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. and the relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account subject to the selected institution's services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale or the relevant Crédit Mutuel entity
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Capital Escrow Account subject to the selected entity's services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for routine euro collections and payments where the provider is an appropriately authorized EU payment institution or electronic-money institution passporting into France. An EMI account is not a bank deposit and generally does not provide deposit-guarantee protection; safeguarded funds are subject to the applicable safeguarding regime. Provider terms may restrict high-volume email, marketing, or technology-related activity, foreign-currency corridors, cash services, and certain jurisdictions. Use a French or EU credit institution for core operating liquidity, payroll, tax payments, and any capital deposit requiring a bank certificate. Verify the provider's authorization, passporting status, safeguarding method, permitted business activities, and account-holder name before relying on the service.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a general rule that SARL directors must appear physically at a bank to open an account. Remote onboarding may be available, subject to the bank's risk assessment, identity-verification controls, e-signature acceptance, and verification of the company, beneficial owners, managers, and business address. Banks may require an in-person meeting or certified documents, particularly for non-resident owners, complex ownership, foreign-source capital, or elevated risk. Confirm requirements directly with the selected bank; remote onboarding is not guaranteed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Email infrastructure and newsletter hosting can be associated with unsolicited bulk messaging, phishing, compromised accounts, or abuse, even where the declared business is legitimate SaaS.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed product and revenue description; customer terms prohibiting spam, phishing, and unlawful content; customer acceptance and suspension controls; consent and unsubscribe procedures; abuse-reporting and incident-response records; domain and sender verification controls; deliverability and complaint monitoring; and a documented escalation process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, or material ownership by non-residents or entities in multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current articles of association, Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence, ownership chart through to natural-person beneficial owners, beneficial-owner filing evidence, identity and address documents, director appointments, and explanations and supporting records for each intermediate entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital or operating funds received from a third party, an unrelated group company, a high-risk jurisdiction, or a source inconsistent with the SARL's expected profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide subscription or shareholder-loan agreements, board or shareholder approvals, bank statements tracing the funds, source-of-wealth evidence where requested, group accounts or audited financial statements, intercompany agreements, and a transaction-specific explanation matching remitter, amount, purpose, and expected cash flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected turnover, payment volume, chargebacks, or cross-border receipts are inconsistent with the business plan or customer base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a forecast by country, currency, payment method, and customer type; sample customer contracts and invoices; Stripe or card-acquirer statements where available; refund and chargeback policies; expected average transaction values; and reconciliation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, payments involving restricted territories, or customers and suppliers whose identity or beneficial ownership cannot be verified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide documented customer and supplier due diligence, sanctions-screening procedures and escalation records, country restrictions, end-user and service-use checks where relevant, and evidence that rejected or blocked transactions are handled under applicable EU and French requirements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route subscriptions and shareholder loans from an account in the investor's or lender's verified name to the SARL's account, using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area or SWIFT for other cross-border payments. State the accurate purpose, such as share capital subscription or shareholder loan, in the transfer reference and provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, corporate approvals, investor identity and ownership documents, and source-of-funds evidence. For a formation capital deposit, use the designated capital-deposit account and obtain the deposit certificate required for registration; release or transfer funds after registration in accordance with the bank's procedure. Do not mislabel equity as a loan or route funds through unrelated third parties. Banks may request supporting documents and may delay or reject transactions under AML, sanctions, or fraud controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments to SEPA beneficiaries and SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly documented by an MT103 message or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for other international payments. Match invoices, purchase orders, contracts, beneficiary details, and payment references; retain evidence of delivery or service where appropriate. For qualifying trade transactions, use documentary letters of credit, collections, or guarantees issued or advised through a bank under agreed documentary terms and applicable ICC rules, such as UCP 600 for documentary credits. Card acquiring and Stripe Billing are collection rails, not substitutes for bank settlement controls. Apply EU sanctions screening, fraud controls, payment reconciliation, and accounting and VAT documentation requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized EU credit institution or investment firm, used to hedge documented or reasonably forecast commercial exposures and subject to the counterparty's suitability, collateral, and documentation requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards where offered lawfully by an appropriately authorized counterparty for an eligible currency exposure; settlement, reporting, and product-governance requirements depend on the instrument and counterparties.

Foreign-exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps with an authorized counterparty to manage documented liquidity or currency exposures, subject to applicable MiFID II, EMIR, collateral, confirmation, reporting, and clearing obligations.
Spot foreign-exchange conversions through an authorized bank or payment provider. Speculative transactions should be separately governed and must not be represented as hedges of commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting (AGOA) to approve financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a tax filing; recorded in the shareholders' minute book and signed by the SARL manager
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any shareholder or the public prosecutor may petition the Commercial Court to order convocation; directors may be held civilly liable for damages caused by late approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the RCS and publication in BODACC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique; publication in BODACC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after AGOA approval; effectively no later than 7 months from fiscal year-end (31 July for 31 December year-end); extension possible on court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Injunction by the President of the Commercial Court with periodic penalty payment (astreinte) up to EUR 10,000; criminal fine up to EUR 1,500 for the manager; repeated non-filing may trigger administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax annual return (liasse fiscale, form 2065 plus 2050-series schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Online filing by 3 May for a 31 December year-end; for other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Article 1728 CGI: 10% if regularized spontaneously, 40% if filed within 30 days of formal notice, 80% if filed after 30 days; plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax installments and final settlement (acomptes et solde d'IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four quarterly installments due 15 December, 15 March, 15 June, and 15 September; final balance due by 15 May following a 31 December year-end, or by the 15th of the 4th month after any other fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid installments or balance incur late-payment interest of 0.2% per month plus a 5% late-payment penalty under Article 1731 CGI; enforcement actions include compulsory recovery and bank seizure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT returns (CA3 monthly or annual simplified declaration CA12)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly regime: VAT return due on the 19th of the following month; simplified regime: annual declaration due by 3 May with prepayments on 15 July and 15 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late VAT payment triggers 0.2% monthly interest plus penalty of 5% (or 0.5% per month) under Articles 1728 and 1730 CGI; deliberate concealment can raise penalties to 80% of assessed VAT

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: EU One Stop Shop (OSS) quarterly VAT return for cross-border B2C digital services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) as OSS reporting authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly return due by the end of the month following each calendar quarter (30 April, 31 July, 31 October, 31 January)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted OSS declarations trigger late-payment interest of 0.2% per month and penalty of 5% of the VAT due; repeated omissions may lead to exclusion from the OSS scheme and VAT registration in each EU member state

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) annual local business tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) acting for the local taxing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Full payment due 15 December of the assessment year; if the annual amount exceeds EUR 3,000, 50% is due 15 June and the balance by 15 December; no separate annual filing is required when the income tax return has been lodged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers an automatic 10% statutory increase (majoration) plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per month; persistent non-payment leads to enforced recovery against bank accounts and business assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer social security declarations via Déclaration Sociale Nominative (DSN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF and affiliated social security bodies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly, on the 5th of the following month for employers with fewer than 50 employees and on the 15th for employers with 50 or more employees; nil declarations are not required when the SARL has no payroll
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing of DSN attracts a late-filing flat-rate penalty and social contribution late-payment penalties of 5% plus 0.2% per month; repeat non-filing can give rise to a lump-sum penalty per employee and criminal liability of the employer in severe cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register (RBE) annual reconciliation and amendment filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the RCS / Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Amendments must be filed within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; annual reconciliation performed at the AGOA and filed concurrently with the annual accounts if a share transfer has occurred; no standalone annual UBO return exists in France
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update RBE exposes the company and manager to fines up to EUR 15,000 and potential imprisonment for deliberate concealment; administrative reminder by the RCS may lead to strike-off proceedings for persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) if, for two consecutive financial years, the SARL exceeds two of these three thresholds: total assets above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (excluding tax) above EUR 8,000,000; average number of permanent employees above 50. Appointment may also be ordered by the Commercial Court at the petition of shareholders holding at least 10% of the capital, or upon the manager's request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under ANC Regulation 2014-03 and the Plan Comptable Général (PCG); the individual statutory accounts of a non-listed SARL must be prepared under French GAAP; IFRS is not available for single-entity statutory accounts of unlisted SARL and applies only to consolidated financial statements of groups when adopted by the parent entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a separate annual UBO certification. The RBE declaration is filed at incorporation and amended within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding structure. At each annual general meeting the manager reconciles the shareholders' register, the share transfer ledger, and the RBE, then files an updated RBE declaration with the RCS whenever share transfers or beneficial ownership changes have occurred during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions d'associés et assemblées générales (minute book of shareholder decisions)
Registre de présence des associés et procurations (attendance and proxy register)
Registre des mouvements de titres et parts sociales (share transfer ledger)
Comptes annuels, journaux comptables, grands livres et pièces justificatives (10-year statutory retention)
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (copy of the RBE declaration filed with the RCS)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 1,100 per year (EUR 300 – EUR 1,000) for commercial domiciliation/registered office and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,800 – USD 10,800 per year (EUR 3,500 – EUR 10,000) for a small-to-mid-cap SARL when a statutory audit is required or voluntarily appointed
